Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 

ROUND OPEN TOP ALUMINIUM CONTAINERS 

FOR LIQUID PESTICIDES 



1. Scope — This standard specifies material, dimensions and testing requirements for round open top 
aluminium containers for the packing of liquid pesticides in nominal quantities of 100. 2S0i 500 and 
1 000 mL 

2. Material 

2.1 The aluminium used for the manufacture of the containers and its loose end shall conform to 
Grade 19500 of IS : 737-1974 'Wrought aluminium and aluminium alloys, sheet and strip (for general 
engineering purposes } ( second revision )'. 

2.2 The seaming compound used shall be compatible with the contents of the container so as to ensure 
a leakproof pack at the end of its expected shelf life. 

3. Dinnansions— The finished dimensions of the extruded or drawn container and its end shall be as 
given in Fig. 1.

4. Workmanship and Finish — The container and the loose end shail be free from any loose metal 
particles, scratches or pit marlcs on the surface. 

B. Liquid Leakage Test — The containers filled with the product or water and seamed all round, 
when kept upside down for 24 hours at ambient conditions shall show no lealcage. 

0. Marking 

8.1 The container shall be embossed or indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name, trade-mark or 
identity mark and any other information as required by the purchaser or the statutory body. 

6.2 Ceff///c<)^/on AfarA//7(|f — The container may also be marked with the Standard Mark. Details are 
available with the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

7. Samplino ** Representative samples for dimensional check and workmanship and finish examination 
shall be drawn as prescribed in IS : 3259*1966 'Methods of sampling of metal containers*. 



EXPLANATORY NOTE 

Round aluminium extruded or deep drawn containers with one end open which is seemed on to 
the container after filling have been tried and proved successful as pilferproof and temperproof packs 
for the liquid pesticides in the country. These containers are to be used with the rocket pourers which 
can be fixed on to the top of the container by piercing through it and gives a spillage-free pouring. 
Each filled container shall be provided with a separate rocket pourer and both shall be destroyed after 
use so as to avoid any accident through reuse of the containers or the pourer. 



Reprography Unit, BIS, New Delhi, India
